_comment: Known-answer cases for the pre-release gate. Every case asserts which dataset must come back, not how many. Thresholds are deliberately loose so catalog drift does not cause false alarms; they are tight enough to catch the failures this file was written for, listed in `regression`.

cases.name: plain multi-term query reaches the portal parser
cases.regression: v0.4.121: text:(...) wrapping cut this to 5 results

cases.name: long keyword query, the shape an LLM generates
cases.regression: v0.4.121: returned 0 results while nine datasets existed

cases.name: boolean query is wrapped where the portal ignores OR
both search tools agree on a boolean query
cases.regression: v0.4.122: find_relevant_datasets never called the parser probe

cases.name: unary operator survives, exclusion not inverted
cases.regression: v0.4.121: escaping turned -rifiuti into a requirement, 7649 -> 398

cases.name: punctuation inside a word is wrapped, dismax reads it as NOT
portal whose text field is empty is never wrapped
cases.regression: wrapping Zurich returns 0 for every query

cases.name: the right dataset ranks first, not just any dataset
cases.regression: v0.4.122: Trento, Martina Franca and Desio outranked the Lecce dataset

cases.name: accented terms contribute to the ranking
cases.regression: \b is ASCII in JS, so qualità scored zero

cases.name: organization filter folds accents before the Solr wildcard
cases.regression: città returned 0 while citta matched 135 datasets

cases.name: tag filter searches beyond the most frequent tags
cases.regression: 53 tags contain citta, none in the top 100, filter said none existed
